papers.title: Tim Berners-Lee: Weaving the Web
papers.excerpt: A critical reflection on Berners-Lee's vision of the World Wide Web as a decentralized, collaborative ecosystem, interrogating its utopian assumptions, Eurocentric biases, and the limits of emergent digital systems.

papers.title: The User Condition: Computer Agency and Digital Behavior
papers.excerpt: An analysis of Silvio Lorusso's critique of digital behavior, automation, and diminishing user agency, drawing on cybernetics, consumer capitalism, and the transformation of action into repetitive behavior.

papers.title: Image as Digital Being
papers.excerpt: An autoethnographic field note examining reliance on visually driven digital environments—particularly multiplayer games—and their effects on attention, habit formation, and immaterial value production.

papers.title: Posthuman Storytelling: Warcraft Series
papers.excerpt: A posthuman analysis of character design and narrative depth in the Warcraft franchise, exploring agency, ethics, and identity through visual storytelling and RPG mechanics.

papers.title: Games as Sites of Meaning
papers.excerpt: An exploration of how meaning, value, and identity are produced in RPG gaming through time investment, digital labor, and posthuman human–machine hybrids.

papers.title: Bugs in Gaming: Classic World of Warcraft
papers.excerpt: A reflective study on technological friction, bugs, and inaccessibility in early World of Warcraft, situating gameplay errors within socio-economic and postcolonial contexts.

papers.title: Evolution of Frictions and Meaning in World of Warcraft
papers.excerpt: An analysis of how automation, refinement, and speedrunning reshape player identity, community, and meaning-making in evolving digital ecosystems.

papers.title: Game Memory in Digital Ecosystems
papers.excerpt: A study of nostalgia, external knowledge systems, and cultural memory in World of Warcraft, examining how digital spaces preserve and reframe historical experience.

papers.title: Posthuman Intimacy: Reconfiguring Desire and Connection in Digital Ecosystems
papers.excerpt: A posthuman analysis of Grindr and Dirty Code, exploring how digital platforms algorithmically mediate desire, commodify intimacy, and reshape embodied relationality.

papers.title: 0.1 — Story-Based Textile Collection
papers.excerpt: A narrative-driven fashion collection exploring coming-of-age, mental illness, inheritance, and vulnerability through experimental textile processes and character-based silhouettes.
